topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: A real estate licensee who enters into an agreement to sell property for an owner is known under Arkansas practice as the "Listing Agent" or:
choice_a: Agent for the Seller
choice_b: Buyer's Agent
choice_c: Dual Agent
choice_d: Escrow Agent
explanation: The AREC Agency Representation brochure explains that a Real Estate Agent who enters into an agreement to sell property for an owner is known as the "Listing Agent" or "Agent for the Seller," and that agent's primary duty is to protect and promote the interests of the seller.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Which of the following is the correct definition of a "Buyer's Agent" under the AREC Agency Representation brochure?
choice_a: A licensee who represents the seller exclusively
choice_b: A licensee who enters into an agreement to represent only the buyer in a real estate transaction
choice_c: A licensee who automatically represents both parties
choice_d: A licensee who may only assist unrepresented sellers
explanation: The brochure defines a Buyer's Agent as a Real Estate Agent who enters into an agreement to only represent the Buyer in a real estate transaction, whose primary duty is to protect and promote the interests of the Buyer.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: A real estate agent who enters into an agreement to represent the seller and also enters into an agreement to represent the buyer in the SAME transaction is known under Arkansas practice as:
choice_a: A subagent
choice_b: A transaction facilitator
choice_c: A Dual Agent
choice_d: An escrow holder
explanation: The AREC brochure defines a Dual Agent as a licensee who enters into an agreement to represent the Seller and also enters into an agreement to represent the Buyer in the same transaction, most frequently occurring when agents within the same firm represent both sides.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 8.3(a), before a licensee may act as a dual agent representing both the seller and buyer in a sale (or lessor and tenant in a lease), what must occur?
choice_a: The principal broker alone may consent on behalf of all parties
choice_b: Only verbal notice to the Commission is required
choice_c: The licensee must obtain errors-and-omissions insurance
choice_d: All parties to the transaction must give their written consent to the dual representation prior to or at the time of execution of the agency contract, listing contract, property management contract, lease, rental agreement, offer and acceptance contract, or other real estate contract
explanation: Regulation 8.3(a) requires that all parties to the transaction give written consent to dual representation prior to or at the time of execution of the applicable contract, and that disclosure be made in the time and manner required by Regulations 8.1 and 8.2.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Arkansas licensee Ray lists a home for Seller Owens through ABC Realty. A different licensee at ABC Realty, under the same principal broker, later signs a buyer representation agreement with Buyer Patel to purchase that same listed home. Under AREC Regulation 8.3, how is this arrangement classified?
choice_a: A dual agency, because both licensees are affiliated with the same principal broker and are representing both sides of the same transaction
choice_b: An illegal subagency arrangement
choice_c: A single agency, because different individual licensees are involved
choice_d: A transaction requiring no disclosure since the licensees are different people
explanation: Regulation 8.3(a) defines dual agency as a licensee representing both the seller and buyer in the same transaction; the brochure clarifies this most frequently occurs when agents within the same firm represent both sides. Arkansas law and rule do not create a separate "designated agency" status distinct from dual agency for same-firm representation of both parties — the Regulation 8.3 written-consent and disclosure procedure applies.
source_note: AREC Commission Regulation 8.3; AREC Agency Representation Brochure (Dec. 2024)

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-108(a)(1), in every real estate transaction involving a licensee, the licensee shall:
choice_a: Provide a home warranty to the buyer
choice_b: Clearly disclose to all parties or their agents which party or parties he or she is representing
choice_c: Refer the parties to an attorney before any showing
choice_d: Waive the commission if requested
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-108(a)(1) requires that in every real estate transaction involving a licensee, the licensee shall clearly disclose to all parties or to their agents which party or parties he or she is representing.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: A.C.A. § 17-42-108(a)(2) provides that a licensee may represent more than one party to a real estate transaction:
choice_a: Under no circumstances whatsoever
choice_b: Only with the approval of a circuit court
choice_c: Pursuant to and subject to rules of the Arkansas Real Estate Commission
choice_d: Only in commercial (non-residential) transactions
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-108(a)(2) states that a licensee may represent more than one party to a real estate transaction pursuant to and subject to rules of the Arkansas Real Estate Commission — those rules being Commission Regulations 8.1 through 8.5.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Per the AREC Agency Representation brochure, the Listing or Seller's Agent's primary duty in a transaction is to:
choice_a: Divide loyalty equally between buyer and seller
choice_b: Remain a neutral facilitator
choice_c: Advise the buyer on negotiating tactics
choice_d: Protect and promote the interests of the seller
explanation: The brochure states that the Listing or Seller's Agent's primary duty is to protect and promote the interests of the Seller.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Per the AREC Agency Representation brochure, an unrepresented buyer dealing with a Seller's Agent should keep which type of information confidential, since the Seller's Agent has a duty to pass it on to the seller?
choice_a: The buyer's highest acceptable offer price and negotiating strategy
choice_b: The property's square footage
choice_c: The property's listing price
choice_d: The name of the buyer's employer
explanation: The brochure advises that as a buyer not represented by a real estate agent, information such as real estate needs or motivations, the highest price the buyer is willing to offer, and negotiating strategies or tactics should be kept confidential from the Seller's Agent, since that agent has a duty to disclose it to the seller.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Per the AREC Agency Representation brochure, an unrepresented seller dealing with a Buyer's Agent should keep which of the following confidential from that agent, since the Buyer's Agent has a duty to disclose it to the buyer?
choice_a: The square footage of the home
choice_b: The seller's lowest acceptable price and reason or motivation for selling
choice_c: The property address
choice_d: The year the home was built
explanation: The brochure advises an unrepresented seller to keep confidential information such as the seller's reason or motivation for selling, the lowest price the seller will accept, and negotiating strategies or tactics, because the Buyer's Agent has a duty to pass such information to the buyer.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-317(b), a licensee representing a seller or lessor does NOT breach a duty to that seller or lessor merely by:
choice_a: Disclosing the seller's minimum acceptable price to a prospective buyer
choice_b: Refusing to present any offers received
choice_c: Showing alternative properties to a prospective buyer or acting as an agent or subagent for other sellers or lessors
choice_d: Withholding the listing from the multiple listing service
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-317(b) states that a licensee does not breach a duty or obligation to a seller or lessor with whom the licensee has an agency relationship by showing alternative properties to a prospective buyer or by acting as an agent or subagent for other sellers or lessors.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-318(b), if a dual or multiple agency relationship has been disclosed under § 17-42-108, a licensee representing a buyer or lessee does not breach a duty to that buyer merely by:
choice_a: Disclosing the buyer's maximum offer to the seller
choice_b: Withholding every offer received from the seller
choice_c: Refusing to negotiate on the buyer's behalf
choice_d: Showing property to other buyers or lessees, or acting as an agent or subagent for other buyers, lessees, sellers, or lessors
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-318(b) provides that, if a dual or multiple agency relationship is disclosed under § 17-42-108, a licensee does not breach a duty to the buyer or lessee by showing property to other buyers or lessees or by acting as an agent or subagent for other buyers, lessees, sellers, or lessors.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: When a licensee acts as an authorized dual agent under A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(1)(B), which of the following is prohibited absent written authorization from the client or a legal requirement?
choice_a: Disclosing to one party confidential information obtained from the other party that may materially compromise that party's negotiating position
choice_b: Presenting any offers at all
choice_c: Showing the property to prospective buyers
choice_d: Communicating with the principal broker
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(2)(J)(ii) permits a dual agent's confidentiality duty to be limited by contract, but disclosure of confidential information that may materially compromise a client's negotiating position remains barred unless required by law or authorized in writing by the client.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Which statement best distinguishes a "customer" from a "client" in Arkansas real estate practice?
choice_a: A customer has a fiduciary agency relationship with the licensee, while a client does not
choice_b: A client has an agency (fiduciary) relationship with the licensee under A.C.A. § 17-42-316, while a customer is a party the licensee deals with in a transaction but does not represent
choice_c: Arkansas law makes no legal distinction between the two
choice_d: Only sellers can be "customers"
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-316(a) applies the common law of agency to "the relationship between a licensee and the licensee's client." A party the licensee deals with but does not represent — a customer — is instead owed honesty and fair dealing rather than the statute's fiduciary duties.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(1)(A), in accepting employment by a client, a licensee pledges:
choice_a: A duty of care limited strictly to inspecting the property's physical condition
choice_b: A duty owed equally to every party in the transaction, client or not
choice_c: A primary duty of absolute fidelity to protect and promote the interests of the client or clients
choice_d: A duty limited strictly to the written contract's four corners
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(1)(A) provides that, except as allowed under the dual-agency waiver provision, in accepting employment by a client, a licensee pledges a primary duty of absolute fidelity to protect and promote the interests of the client or clients.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(2), a licensee's fiduciary duties to a client include the obligation to:
choice_a: Guarantee that the sale will close
choice_b: Provide legal advice directly to the client
choice_c: Waive confidentiality upon the request of any third party
choice_d: Account in a timely manner for all moneys and property received in which the client has or may have an interest
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(2)(I) lists among the licensee's duties the obligation to account in a timely manner for all moneys and property received in which the client has or may have an interest.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Which of the following is listed among a licensee's statutory fiduciary duties under A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(2)?
choice_a: Disclose to the client material facts of the transaction the licensee is aware of or should be aware of, that are not confidential information under a current or prior agency relationship
choice_b: Guarantee financing approval for the client
choice_c: Personally inspect the property using expert testing equipment
choice_d: Set the sale price without client input
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(2)(G) requires the licensee to disclose to the client material facts of the transaction that the licensee is aware of or should be aware of, and that are not confidential information under a current or prior agency or dual agency relationship.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(2)(H), when material matters arise that are outside the scope of a licensee's expertise, the licensee's duty is to:
choice_a: Resolve the matter personally regardless of expertise
choice_b: Advise the client to obtain expert advice concerning material matters when necessary or appropriate
choice_c: Ignore the matter unless the client raises it first
choice_d: Refer the client only to the licensee's own personal attorney
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(2)(H) requires the licensee to advise the client to obtain expert advice concerning material matters when necessary or appropriate.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-316(c), the fiduciary duties required of a licensee under that section:
choice_a: May always be waived by a client in writing
choice_b: May never be discussed with the client
choice_c: May not be waived by a client, except as provided for authorized dual agency and the limited confidentiality carve-out
choice_d: Apply only to buyer's agents
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-316(c) provides that, except as provided in subdivisions (b)(1)(B) and (b)(2)(J)(ii) — the dual agency fidelity waiver and limited confidentiality exception — the duties required of a licensee under this section may not be waived by a client.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(1)(B), which clients may contractually waive the licensee's primary duty of absolute fidelity?
choice_a: Any single client, at any time
choice_b: A seller client only
choice_c: A buyer client only
choice_d: Multiple clients represented by the same licensee who have consented to dual agency
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(1)(B) provides that multiple clients who are represented by the licensee and have consented to dual agency may contractually waive the licensee's primary duty of absolute fidelity described in subdivision (b)(1)(A).

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: A licensee's duty to "refrain from disclosing any confidential information" under A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(2)(J) may be limited by contract in which circumstance?
choice_a: When the licensee is an authorized dual agent under § 17-42-316(b)(1)(B)
choice_b: Whenever the client requests it verbally
choice_c: Never, under any circumstance
choice_d: Only after the transaction closes
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(2)(J)(ii) states that disclosure of confidential information may be limited by contract when a licensee is an authorized dual agent under subdivision (b)(1)(B), though disclosure that would materially compromise a client's negotiating position still requires legal necessity or written client authorization.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(2)(K), a licensee must refrain from disclosing confidential information to:
choice_a: The licensee's own principal broker
choice_b: A licensee who is not an agent of the client
choice_c: The client's spouse
choice_d: The title company handling closing
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-316(b)(2)(K) requires a licensee to refrain from disclosing confidential information to a licensee who is not an agent of the client, such as the licensee representing the opposing party.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-319(a), a licensee is relieved of performing the duties required under § 17-42-317 or § 17-42-318 only if:
choice_a: The Commission grants a blanket exemption
choice_b: More than 90 days have passed since the listing began
choice_c: The client agrees to waive those duties and signs a written waiver of duties statement meeting the statute's requirements
choice_d: The client is a repeat customer of the firm
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-319(a) provides that a licensee shall perform the duties required under § 17-42-317 or § 17-42-318 unless the client agrees to waive these duties and signs a waiver of duties statement containing specific required content.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-319(a)(3), a written waiver of agency duties statement must include specific language, in what minimum type size, informing the client that the licensee will not perform the waived duties and that the client may need to hire other professionals?
choice_a: 8-point regular type
choice_b: 6-point italic type
choice_c: 12-point regular type
choice_d: 10-point boldface type
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-319(a)(3) requires the "Agreement to Waive" language to appear in at least 10-point boldface type, stating that the licensee will not perform the initialed duties and that the client may need to hire other professionals such as an attorney.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-319(b)(2), even where a client has signed a valid waiver of duties statement, a licensee representing a buyer or lessee remains authorized to:
choice_a: Present offers to buy, lease, or rent real property directly to the licensee's principal, notwithstanding the waiver or a conflicting statute or rule
choice_b: Withhold all offers from the client
choice_c: Keep earnest money in a personal account
choice_d: Refuse to communicate with the client entirely
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-319(b)(2) provides that a licensee for a buyer or lessee remains authorized to present offers to buy, lease, or rent real property directly to the licensee's principal, notwithstanding a waiver under subsection (a) or a conflicting statute or rule.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-319(b)(1), if a licensee enters into an agency relationship containing waivers of duties, the licensee must take reasonable efforts to inform other licensees that:
choice_a: The waiver applies to the Commission's disciplinary jurisdiction
choice_b: Moneys of others, including earnest money, advance fees, or security deposits, are not to be transmitted or kept by the waiving licensee, notwithstanding other applicable statutes and rules
choice_c: The client no longer needs any written contract
choice_d: The waiver eliminates the need for an agency agreement altogether
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-319(b)(1) requires reasonable efforts to inform other licensees that any moneys of others — including earnest money, advance fees, or security deposits — are not to be transmitted or kept by the licensee who has waived agency duties, notwithstanding other applicable statutes and rules.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Per AREC Commission Regulation 8.5(a), a licensee's "obligation of absolute fidelity to the interest of the client or clients is primary, but does not relieve a licensee from" what other equally binding obligation?
choice_a: The obligation to guarantee the sale price
choice_b: The obligation to represent both parties equally as clients
choice_c: The equally binding obligation of dealing honestly with all parties to the transaction
choice_d: The obligation to waive commission if a customer requests it
explanation: Regulation 8.5(a) provides that in accepting employment as an agent, a licensee pledges to protect and promote the interests of the client; this obligation of absolute fidelity is primary, but does not relieve the licensee of the equally binding obligation of dealing honestly with all parties to the transaction.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Per AREC Commission Regulation 8.5(c), when acting as agent in the sale or management of property, a licensee shall not accept any commission, rebate, profit, payment, or other valuable consideration from any source in connection with the property without:
choice_a: Verbal notice to the Commission
choice_b: A separate written contract with a third party
choice_c: Approval from the buyer only
choice_d: Full written disclosure to the party represented by the licensee
explanation: Regulation 8.5(c) requires full written disclosure to the party represented by the licensee before accepting any commission, rebate, profit, payment, or other valuable consideration from any source in connection with the property.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 8.1(c), governing a seller's or lessor's agent, disclosure of the agency relationship to the buyer or lessee must be made:
choice_a: Before the buyer or lessee signs any document related to the transaction, such as an offer, lease, or rental agreement
choice_b: Only after closing
choice_c: Within 30 days after the listing agreement is signed
choice_d: Only if requested by the buyer's attorney
explanation: Regulation 8.1(c) requires that disclosure must be made before the buyer or lessee signs any document related to the transaction, such as an offer or lease or rental agreement.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 8.2(a)(1), a licensee acting solely as agent for a buyer or lessee must disclose that agency relationship to the seller, lessor, or their licensed agent:
choice_a: Only at the closing table
choice_b: At the first contact with the seller, lessor, or the agent of the seller or lessor
choice_c: Only if the seller specifically asks
choice_d: Within the buyer representation agreement only
explanation: Regulation 8.2(a)(1) requires a buyer's or lessee's agent to disclose the agency relationship to the seller, lessor, or their licensed agent at the first contact with the seller, lessor, or the agent of the seller or lessor.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulations 8.1(b) and 8.2(b), agency disclosure:
choice_a: Must always be exclusively written from the outset, with no oral component permitted
choice_b: Is required only in commercial transactions
choice_c: May initially be made orally and reduced to writing at a convenient time, with evidence of the disclosure maintained by the licensee, subject to the applicable timing requirements
choice_d: Is entirely optional at the licensee's discretion
explanation: Regulations 8.1(b) and 8.2(b) both provide that disclosure shall be in writing but may initially be made orally and reduced to writing at a convenient time, subject to the timing requirements of 8.1(c) and 8.2(c), with evidence of the disclosure maintained by the licensee.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 8.1(a)(1), when a licensee acts solely as agent for a seller or lessor, the disclosure to the prospective buyer or lessee should be timed so as to:
choice_a: Occur only after an offer has been accepted
choice_b: Occur simultaneously with closing
choice_c: Occur only via certified mail
choice_d: Avoid, to the extent possible, eliciting or receiving confidential information from the prospective buyer or lessee, such as negotiating strategy, financial situation, or real estate needs, before disclosure is made
explanation: Regulation 8.1(a)(1) requires disclosure to be made in a timely manner under the circumstances so as to avoid, to the extent possible, eliciting or receiving confidential information from the prospective buyer or lessee before the disclosure occurs.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulations 8.1(a)(2) and 8.2(a)(2), when agency disclosure is made to the licensed agent of the opposite party rather than directly to that party, what duty arises?
choice_a: That licensee's duty to convey the disclosure to their own client in a timely manner
choice_b: No further duty arises
choice_c: The disclosure becomes legally void
choice_d: The Commission must be separately notified in writing
explanation: Both Regulations 8.1(a)(2) and 8.2(a)(2) state that when disclosure is made to the licensed agent of the other party, it is that licensee's duty to convey the disclosure to their own client (the buyer, lessee, seller, or lessor) in a timely manner.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Per the AREC Agency Representation Disclosure Form described in the Commission's brochure, "Option 1" of the form is used when:
choice_a: The agent represents all parties under a separate written agency agreement
choice_b: The real estate agent does not represent the person signing, but represents only the buyer or only the seller, and that non-represented person signs acknowledging the disclosure
choice_c: No agency relationship exists at all in the transaction
choice_d: The transaction involves a lease only
explanation: The brochure's disclosure form Option 1 is initialed when the named agent does not represent the signer but represents only the buyer or only the seller; the brochure's FAQ notes the person NOT represented should sign as receiving the disclosure in that scenario.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 8.4, a licensee who fails to disclose the licensee's agency relationship in the time and manner required by the agency disclosure regulations is subject to:
choice_a: No consequence, since disclosure is discretionary
choice_b: Automatic license revocation with no hearing
choice_c: Sanctions under A.C.A. § 17-42-312
choice_d: A refund of commission only
explanation: Regulation 8.4 provides that a licensee who fails to disclose the licensee's agency relationship in the time and manner required by these regulations shall be subject to sanctions under A.C.A. § 17-42-312.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: A.C.A. § 17-42-108(b) provides that the timing, method, and other requirements of the agency disclosure, and the consequences of failing to make disclosure in accordance with such requirements, shall be established by:
choice_a: Each individual principal broker
choice_b: The buyer's attorney
choice_c: The Arkansas Realtors Association
choice_d: The Arkansas Real Estate Commission
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-108(b) provides that the timing, method, and other requirements of disclosure shall be established by the Commission, which shall also determine the consequences of failure to make disclosure in accordance with those requirements.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Per the AREC Agency Representation brochure's FAQ, is a licensee required to use the Commission's specific Agency Representation pamphlet and disclosure form?
choice_a: No; it is a tool licensees may use to help ensure compliance with Commission Regulations 8.1, 8.2, and 8.3, but alternative forms or procedures may be used
choice_b: Yes; use of the exact form is mandatory under A.C.A. § 17-42-108
choice_c: Yes, but only for lease transactions
choice_d: No disclosure procedure is ever required in Arkansas
explanation: The brochure's FAQ #1 states that the AREC Agency Representation pamphlet and disclosure form is a tool licensees may use to ensure compliance with Regulations 8.1, 8.2, and 8.3, and that an agent may use alternative forms or procedures to comply with those regulations.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Per the AREC Agency Representation brochure, when "Option 2" of the disclosure form applies — where the agent represents all parties under a separate written agency agreement to which they previously consented — the brochure instructs that:
choice_a: Only the buyer needs to sign
choice_b: All persons receiving the disclosure should each sign a form
choice_c: Only the principal broker needs to sign
choice_d: No signature of any kind is required
explanation: The brochure's FAQ #3 states that when Option 2 of the disclosure form is applicable, all persons receiving the disclosure should each sign a form.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 10.2, what must a licensee include on all written agency agreements or contracts (such as listing and buyer representation agreements) or extensions thereof?
choice_a: A notarized signature
choice_b: A minimum commission rate
choice_c: A specific determinable duration or a specific expiration date
choice_d: A property survey
explanation: Regulation 10.2 requires a licensee to put a specific determinable duration or a specific expiration date on all written agency agreements or contracts, or any extensions thereof, giving listing and buyer representation agreements as examples.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 10.10(a), for the protection of the public and all parties with whom the licensee deals, a licensee shall ensure that:
choice_a: Verbal agreements are preferred over written ones
choice_b: Only the principal broker retains a copy of any agreement
choice_c: Agency agreements renew automatically without any expiration
choice_d: The exact agreement of the parties regarding real estate is in writing, and that clients and other parties receive signed copies of such agreements
explanation: Regulation 10.10(a) requires that, for the protection of the public and of all parties with whom the licensee deals, the exact agreement of the parties regarding real estate be in writing, and that clients and other parties receive copies of such agreements signed by all parties.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 10.13(b), before entering into a new agency agreement with a client when the licensee has reason to believe an existing exclusive agency agreement is already in force, the licensee must first:
choice_a: Communicate with the other principal broker who holds the existing agreement to confirm its existence, and if it exists, notify the client in writing to consult an attorney regarding the risk of liability for two separate commissions
choice_b: Immediately terminate the client relationship
choice_c: File a complaint against the client with the Commission
choice_d: Ignore the prior agreement since it does not affect the new one
explanation: Regulation 10.13(b) requires a licensee who has reason to believe an existing exclusive agency agreement is in force to first confirm its existence with the other principal broker, and, if confirmed, to notify the client in writing to consult an attorney about the risk of being liable for two separate commissions.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 10.13(a), if a firm holds an exclusive listing contract on a property, a selling licensee from another firm must obtain permission before:
choice_a: Advertising any property in the multiple listing service
choice_b: Contacting the seller directly about showing the property or negotiating the sale, without going through the listing firm or its authorized representative
choice_c: Showing any home in the same neighborhood
choice_d: Cooperating on any transaction whatsoever
explanation: Regulation 10.13(a) provides that when a firm holds an exclusive listing contract, the selling licensee shall not contact the seller about showing the property or negotiating the sale without prior permission from the listing firm or its authorized representative.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 10.11 (Self Dealing), a licensee who wants to buy, rent, or lease property for himself, or for an entity in which he has an interest, must first:
choice_a: Obtain Commission pre-approval
choice_b: Reduce his commission to zero
choice_c: Make full written disclosure to the buyer or seller, as the case may be, of the exact facts of his licensure and his personal interest, before the sales, rental, or lease contract is entered into
choice_d: Simply mention it verbally at the closing table
explanation: Regulation 10.11 requires licensees to make full written disclosure of their licensure and personal interest to the buyer or seller before the sales, rental, or lease contract is entered into, when buying, selling, renting, or leasing property for themselves or an entity in which they have an interest.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 10.12(a), all offers received on a specific property shall be:
choice_a: Held by the selling licensee until closing
choice_b: Disclosed only to the Commission
choice_c: Discarded if below the asking price
choice_d: Promptly presented to the seller by the listing firm or another licensee designated by an authorized representative of the listing firm
explanation: Regulation 10.12(a) requires that all offers received on a specific property be promptly presented to the seller by the listing firm or another licensee designated by an authorized representative of the listing firm.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 10.12(b), every offer received on a property must be signed by:
choice_a: The licensee who receives it and that licensee's supervising broker
choice_b: Only the buyer
choice_c: Only the seller's attorney
choice_d: The Commission's executive director
explanation: Regulation 10.12(b) requires every offer received to be signed by the licensee who receives it and by that licensee's supervising broker, with acceptances similarly signed by the listing licensee and that licensee's supervising broker.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 10.13(c), signs offering or advertising a property may be placed on the property:
choice_a: At any time regardless of listing status
choice_b: Only during the existence of a listing agreement, unless otherwise authorized by the owner
choice_c: Only after closing
choice_d: Only with the Commission's prior approval
explanation: Regulation 10.13(c) provides that signs offering or advertising a property may be on the property only during the existence of a listing agreement, unless otherwise authorized by the owner.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: A.C.A. § 17-42-311(a)(8) identifies as a prohibited act:
choice_a: Advertising a property with the firm's name included
choice_b: Accompanying a listing licensee to a showing
choice_c: Acting for more than one party in a transaction without the knowledge of all parties for whom the licensee acts, or accepting compensation for such acts from anyone other than the licensed principal broker under whom the licensee is licensed
choice_d: Delivering a signed copy of a contract to the client
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-311(a)(8) prohibits acting for more than one party in a transaction without the knowledge of all parties for whom the licensee acts, or accepting a commission or valuable consideration from anyone other than the licensed principal broker under whom the licensee is licensed.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 10.10(c), citing Pope County Bar Association, Inc. v. Suggs, real estate forms used by licensees in the regular course of business (including agency and listing agreements) must be:
choice_a: Drafted personally by the Commission's executive director
choice_b: Filed with the county recorder
choice_c: Reviewed by a certified appraiser
choice_d: Approved by a licensed Arkansas attorney prior to use
explanation: Regulation 10.10(c), citing Pope County Bar Association, Inc. v. Suggs, 624 S.W.2d 828 (1981), requires that real estate forms used by licensees in the regular course of business be approved by a licensed Arkansas attorney prior to use, with the licensee responsible for providing evidence of that approval upon Commission request.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-311(a)(4), which act constitutes a prohibited violation subject to disciplinary action?
choice_a: Making any substantial misrepresentation
choice_b: Advertising a listed property with the firm's name
choice_c: Delivering signed contract copies to a client
choice_d: Filing a required trust account reconciliation
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-311(a)(4) lists "making any substantial misrepresentation" as a prohibited act subject to disciplinary action under § 17-42-312.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-311(a)(5), a licensee violates the license law by:
choice_a: Attending continuing education
choice_b: Making, printing, publishing, or knowingly permitting the publication of false statements, descriptions, or promises reasonably likely to induce or persuade a person to act on them
choice_c: Renewing an inactive license
choice_d: Reporting a violation to the Commission
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-311(a)(5) prohibits making, printing, publishing, distributing, or knowingly permitting the making, printing, publication, or distribution of false statements, descriptions, or promises of such character as to reasonably induce, persuade, or influence any person to act thereon.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 10.6, a licensee's duty regarding "Knowledge of Property" requires the licensee to:
choice_a: Hire a licensed home inspector for every listing
choice_b: Guarantee the absence of all defects
choice_c: Exert reasonable efforts to ascertain facts material to the value or desirability of a property for which the licensee accepts the agency, so as to avoid intentional or negligent misrepresentation to the public
choice_d: Rely solely on the seller's verbal assurances without further inquiry
explanation: Regulation 10.6 requires a licensee to exert reasonable efforts to ascertain facts material to the value or desirability of every property for which the licensee accepts the agency, so that the licensee is informed about the property's condition and able to avoid intentional or negligent misrepresentation to the public.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Per AREC Commission Regulation 8.5(b), in any offering or advertisement of property, a licensee shall not quote a price that is:
choice_a: Rounded to the nearest thousand dollars
choice_b: Below fair market value
choice_c: Above fair market value
choice_d: Other than the price agreed upon with the owner as the offering price
explanation: Regulation 8.5(b) provides that a licensee shall not offer or advertise property without authority, and that in any offering or advertisement the price quoted must not be other than that agreed upon with the owners as the offering price.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: If the Arkansas Real Estate Commission determines in a disciplinary hearing under A.C.A. § 17-42-406 that a licensee's misrepresentation caused damages to an aggrieved party, the Commission's authority to award damages from the Real Estate Recovery Fund is limited to:
choice_a: Actual, compensatory damages only, excluding punitive or exemplary damages and interest on damages
choice_b: Punitive damages up to $100,000
choice_c: Treble damages
choice_d: Whatever amount the injured party demands
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-407(a) limits the Commission's jurisdiction and authority to award damages under § 17-42-406 to actual, compensatory damages, and bars the award of punitive or exemplary damages or interest on damages.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-406(a)(4), if a licensee found liable for misrepresentation does not pay the Commission-ordered damages within 30 days and the order is not appealed, the Commission shall pay the aggrieved party from the Real Estate Recovery Fund up to what maximum amount for any one violation or continuing series of violations?
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-406(a)(4)(A) caps the Recovery Fund's payment at $25,000 for any one violation or continuing series of violations, regardless of the number of licensees who participated.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-406(c), the Real Estate Recovery Fund's total exposure with respect to the acts of any one licensee, or any group of related claims, is capped at:
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-406(c) provides that nothing in the subchapter shall obligate the fund for an amount in excess of a total of $75,000 with respect to the acts of any one licensee or any group of related claims.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-312(a)(4), sanctions the Commission may impose for a proven violation such as misrepresentation include all of the following EXCEPT:
choice_a: Suspension, revocation, or denial of the license
choice_b: A penalty of not more than $1,000 per violation
choice_c: Payment of restitution or damages appropriate to the case
choice_d: Automatic imprisonment for up to one year
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-312(a)(4) authorizes sanctions such as license suspension, revocation, or denial; a penalty of not more than $1,000 per violation; educational or examination requirements; conditions or restrictions on practice; and restitution or damages — but criminal imprisonment is not among the Commission's administrative sanctions under this section.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-311(a)(7), which of the following is a prohibited act subject to disciplinary sanctions?
choice_a: Committing any act involving violence, fraud, dishonesty, untruthfulness, or untrustworthiness
choice_b: Attending an AREC-approved continuing education course
choice_c: Maintaining a monthly trust account reconciliation
choice_d: Displaying a required firm sign
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-311(a)(7) prohibits committing any act involving violence, fraud, dishonesty, untruthfulness, or untrustworthiness, which encompasses misrepresentation toward clients and customers alike.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Following payment of a claim from the Real Estate Recovery Fund due to a licensee's misrepresentation, A.C.A. § 17-42-409 provides that the licensee's license shall be:
choice_a: Left unaffected
choice_b: Immediately suspended until the licensee completely reimburses the Commission for the payment, plus interest not to exceed 10% per annum
choice_c: Permanently revoked with no path to reinstatement
choice_d: Automatically transferred to another principal broker
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-409(3) provides that upon payment from the Recovery Fund, the licensee's license shall be immediately suspended until fully reimbursing the Commission for the payment plus interest at a rate the Commission sets, not to exceed 10% per annum.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-317(a)(2), when representing a seller or lessor, a licensee must accept delivery of and present an offer to the seller or lessor:
choice_a: Only if the offer meets or exceeds the listing price
choice_b: Only after any existing contract falls through
choice_c: In a timely manner, regardless of whether the property is subject to a contract of sale, lease, or letter of intent to lease
choice_d: Only with the buyer's attorney present
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-317(a)(2) requires a licensee representing a seller or lessor to accept delivery of and present an offer to the seller or lessor in a timely manner, regardless of whether the property is subject to a contract of sale, lease, or letter of intent to lease.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-317(a)(1)(B), when representing a seller who already has an accepted contract of sale, lease, or letter of intent to lease on the property, is the licensee obligated to keep seeking additional offers?
choice_a: Yes, always, regardless of the seller's wishes
choice_b: No, seeking additional offers is prohibited entirely once a contract exists
choice_c: Only if a second offer arrives unsolicited
choice_d: No, unless the seller or lessor requests it
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-317(a)(1)(B) provides that, unless requested by the seller or lessor, the licensee is not obligated to seek additional offers if the property is already subject to a contract of sale, lease, or letter of intent to lease.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-318(a)(4), when representing a buyer or lessee, a licensee must, in a timely manner:
choice_a: Present an offer to purchase or lease to the seller or lessor or their agent, regardless of whether the property is already subject to a contract of sale, lease, or letter of intent to lease, and accept delivery of and present any counteroffers to the buyer or lessee
choice_b: Wait until the current listing expires before presenting any offer
choice_c: Withhold the offer until the buyer's financing is fully approved
choice_d: Present the offer only if it exceeds the asking price
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-318(a)(4) requires a licensee representing a buyer or lessee, in a timely manner, to present an offer to purchase or lease regardless of whether the property is subject to an existing contract of sale, lease, or letter of intent to lease, and to accept delivery of and present any counteroffers to the buyer or lessee.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-317(a)(3)(B), within the scope of knowledge required for licensure, a licensee representing a seller must provide the seller information regarding:
choice_a: The buyer's full personal financial statements
choice_b: Offers or counteroffers of which the licensee has actual knowledge
choice_c: Confidential negotiating strategy disclosed by the buyer's agent
choice_d: Only offers that meet or exceed the listing price
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-317(a)(3)(B) requires a licensee, within the scope of knowledge required for licensure, to provide information to the seller or lessor regarding offers or counteroffers of which the licensee has actual knowledge.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: When multiple written offers are received on the same listed property in Arkansas, under AREC Commission Regulation 10.12(a) combined with the seller-agency duties in A.C.A. § 17-42-317(a)(2), the listing licensee's obligation is to:
choice_a: Select which offer to present based on the licensee's own preference
choice_b: Present only the highest-priced offer
choice_c: Promptly present all offers received to the seller so the seller, not the licensee, can decide how to respond
choice_d: Reject all but one offer without seller input
explanation: Regulation 10.12(a) requires all offers received to be promptly presented to the seller, and § 17-42-317(a)(2) requires timely presentation of offers; together these require the licensee to present every offer received and let the seller decide, not to filter or select on the licensee's own initiative.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-318(a)(1)(B), is a licensee representing a buyer obligated to keep searching for additional properties once the buyer has already contracted to purchase, or extended a letter of intent to lease, a suitable property?
choice_a: Yes, in all cases
choice_b: No, seeking additional properties is barred entirely once under contract
choice_c: Only if the seller requests it
choice_d: No, unless the client requests it
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-318(a)(1)(B) provides that, unless requested by the client, the licensee is not obligated to seek additional purchase or lease possibilities if the buyer or lessee has already contracted to purchase or lease, or extended a letter of intent to lease, suitable property.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under AREC Commission Regulation 10.13(a), if a selling licensee (not the listing firm) receives an offer on an exclusively listed property, that offer must be presented to the firm holding the exclusive listing contract:
choice_a: Not later than the close of the next business day after receipt of the offer
choice_b: Within 30 calendar days
choice_c: Only upon the buyer's written demand
choice_d: Never; the selling licensee presents it directly to the seller
explanation: Regulation 10.13(a) requires that any offers received by the selling licensee be presented to the firm holding the exclusive listing contract not later than the close of the next business day after receipt of the offer, with earnest money forwarded to the listing firm's trust account.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Per AREC Commission Regulation 8.5(a), even though a licensee's primary fiduciary obligation of absolute fidelity runs to the client, the licensee remains subject to what additional, equally binding obligation toward all parties (including customers) in the transaction?
choice_a: An obligation to negotiate on the customer's behalf
choice_b: The equally binding obligation of dealing honestly with all parties to the transaction
choice_c: An obligation to place the customer's interests above the client's
choice_d: No further obligation exists toward non-clients
explanation: Regulation 8.5(a) states that the primary duty of fidelity to a client does not relieve a licensee of the equally binding obligation of dealing honestly with all parties to the transaction, including unrepresented customers.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: A.C.A. § 17-42-311(a)(4) and (5), prohibiting substantial misrepresentation and false statements reasonably likely to induce a person to act, apply:
choice_a: Only to statements made to the licensee's own client
choice_b: Only in commercial transactions
choice_c: To dealings with any party to a transaction, whether or not that party is the licensee's client
choice_d: Only after a written contract has been signed
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-311(a)(4) and (5) contain no limitation to clients; they prohibit substantial misrepresentation and false statements or promises directed at "any person," reaching dealings with customers as well as clients.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under the AREC Agency Representation brochure, when a licensee represents only the seller and deals with an unrepresented buyer (a customer), the licensee's duty to that buyer is best described as:
choice_a: A full fiduciary duty identical to the duty owed the seller
choice_b: No duty whatsoever
choice_c: A duty to negotiate the lowest possible price for the buyer
choice_d: A duty of honest dealing and disclosure, distinct from and narrower than the fiduciary duties owed to the represented seller client
explanation: The brochure and Regulation 8.5(a) together establish that a customer receives honest dealing rather than the fiduciary duties (loyalty, confidentiality, advocacy) owed exclusively to the represented client.
source_note: AREC Agency Representation Brochure (Dec. 2024); AREC Commission Regulation 8.5(a)

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-311(a)(11), a licensee may face disciplinary action for:
choice_a: Being unworthy or incompetent to act as a licensee in such a manner as to safeguard the interests of the public
choice_b: Cooperating with another firm on a sale
choice_c: Advertising with the firm's name included
choice_d: Disclosing agency representation in writing
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-311(a)(11) prohibits being unworthy or incompetent to act as a real estate broker or salesperson in such a manner as to safeguard the interests of the public, a standard that applies to a licensee's conduct toward clients and customers alike.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Consistent with the duty of honest dealing owed to all parties under AREC Commission Regulation 8.5(a), how does Commission Regulation 10.6 (Knowledge of Property) most directly support the treatment of customers?
choice_a: It allows a licensee to withhold a known material latent defect from an unrepresented buyer without consequence
choice_b: It requires the licensee's duty to exert reasonable efforts to know material facts about the property, so as to avoid intentional or negligent misrepresentation "to the public," to extend to dealings with customers, not just clients
choice_c: It makes only the seller responsible for disclosing property defects
choice_d: It applies only to buyer's agents
explanation: Regulation 10.6 frames the misrepresentation risk in terms of the licensee's duty to "the public," not merely to the licensee's own client, reinforcing that the duty to avoid misrepresenting material facts extends to customers as well as clients.
source_note: AREC Commission Regulation 10.6; AREC Commission Regulation 8.5(a)

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Under A.C.A. § 17-42-311(a)(10), advertising in a false, misleading, or deceptive manner is prohibited. This rule protects:
choice_a: Only the licensee's own client
choice_b: Only competing brokers
choice_c: Members of the public generally, including prospective customers who are not the licensee's clients
choice_d: Only the Commission's enforcement staff
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-311(a)(10) bars false, misleading, or deceptive advertising without limiting the prohibition to communications with clients, protecting members of the public — including customers who see the advertising but are not represented by the licensee.

topic: Client and Customer Relationships and Agency Disclosures
question: Which best summarizes the difference between the duties Arkansas law imposes on a licensee toward a "client" versus toward a "customer"?
choice_a: There is no difference; both receive identical fiduciary duties
choice_b: Customers receive greater legal protection than clients
choice_c: Clients receive only the duty of honest dealing, while customers receive full fiduciary duties
choice_d: A client receives the full fiduciary duties enumerated in A.C.A. § 17-42-316 (loyalty, confidentiality, accounting, and the like), while a customer, though not owed those fiduciary duties, is still owed honesty and fair dealing, including freedom from misrepresentation of material facts, under A.C.A. § 17-42-311 and Commission Regulation 8.5(a)
explanation: A.C.A. § 17-42-316 establishes a fiduciary agency relationship only between a licensee and that licensee's client, while A.C.A. § 17-42-311 (barring misrepresentation and dishonest dealing) and Regulation 8.5(a) (requiring honest dealing with all parties) impose a baseline of honesty and fair dealing that protects customers even absent an agency relationship.
